statement: Prompting claim C1 (supported): Over matched informal/formal prompt pairs, informal token count is lower in more than half of pairs and in the pooled sum. Numbers: The source is workshop/ath_prompts/measure/results.md, which uses Qwen2.5-0.5B token counts. I recomputed the 10 typed prompt pairs with /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c7c2895f-eb04-517d-b538-6d0d59d567a9/scratchpad/qq/c1.py. The informal prompt has fewer tokens in 7 of 10 pairs. Pooled, informal has 236 tokens and formal has 267. Both parts of the claim hold. Two pairs go the other way: 00:43 (83 vs 79) and 00:44 (23 vs 21). One pair ties: 06:19 (5 vs 5). The prefs block is a single pair, and it also goes the other way: 226 vs 204. With prefs added, the pooled sums are 462 vs 471, so informal is still lower

Prompting claim C2 (supported): Informal bits per character exceed formal in at least 9 of 10 pairs at every model size, Wilcoxon p<0.05. Numbers: My recount from workshop/ath_prompts/measure/heavy/data/*.json gives these counts of pairs where informal bits/char is higher than formal: 0.5B 10 of 10, p=0.0020; 1.5B 10 of 10, p=0.0020; 3B 9 of 10, p=0.0039; 7B-q4 10 of 10, p=0.0020. The p values are exact two-sided Wilcoxon tests. These match workshop/ath_prompts/measure/heavy/results.md (B1c). That file gives pooled bits/char, informal vs formal: 2.11/1.46 (0.5B), 1.99/1.42 (1.5B), 2.11/1.44 (3B), 2.11/1.59 (7B-q4). workshop/ath_prompts/measure/results.md gives 6.01 vs 4.64 nats/token at 0.5B. All four sizes meet the bar of at least 9 of 10 pairs with p<0.05. Cavea

Prompting claim C3 (untested): For the same task, informal asks yield an equal or higher success rate and at least 1 fewer correction per task than formal asks, over many trials. Numbers: The repo has no numbers on task success or corrections. /home/user/pnp-general/ath_prompts/measure/results.md compares 10 informal prompts with formal rewrites. It reports token count and loss only. Informal had fewer tokens in 7 of 10 prompts and lower total loss in 5 of 10. Mean loss was 6.01 for informal and 4.64 nats/token for formal. Line 100 says: "Token count and loss are not task success; nothing here says either version gets the instruction followed better." /home/user/pnp-general/ath_prompts/measure/heavy/results.md line 228 says the same: "Surprisal is not task success." The repo at /home/user/pnp-general has no formal-register session to compare against. The boards/ folder and BOARD.md could only give quote counts for the informal side. Prompting claim C5 (untested): Projects with per-task boards show fewer duplicated tasks, merge conflicts and questions to Addison per checked finding than projects without. There are 82 merge commits. 3 commit messages mention "conflict" and 8 mention "duplicate". These are keyword hits, not measured conflicts or duplicate tasks. Prompting claim C6 (untested): Messages sent between seats per completed task fall after one-owner boards were introduced. Numbers: The repo has only two message logs. /home/user/pnp-general/one-not/tools/stat_search/INBOX.json has 6 messages. /home/user/pnp-general/one-not/tools/l951_charging/INBOX.json has 8 messages. All 14 are dated 2026-11-23. That is one day only, so there is no "before one-owner boards" period to compare against. Nothing links these messages to completed tasks either. I counted them with an inline python3 one-liner (no script file). The git log of boards/ records edits, not messages.

Prompting claim C7 (untested): In a regression c(s) = a + b|F(s)| + d|l(s)|, |F(s)| explains most variance; narrow Sonnet seats cost about 77-100k tokens each. Numbers: The cost per seat is consistent with the claim. The regression is not tested. Source /home/user/pnp-general/ath_prompts/measure/cost_per_result.md, line 12: plain Sonnet one-lemma seats, 13 seats, 15 lemmas, 1,165,505 tokens in total, 89,654 tokens per seat, and 77,700 per checked lemma. Line 21: a 32 s seat (C1) used 76,792 tokens and a 156 s seat (B8) used 86,424. So tokens barely track time. Line 45: across 18 seats in order the slope is +1,523 tokens per seat, r = 0.22. That is no clear trend with repo size. Line 50: heavier multi-lemma lines cost 130-200k. Source /home/user/pnp-general/at

Prompting claim C8 (toss-up): Slope of Sonnet tokens per checked result vs commit count is not different from 0, and C(R) stays below a fixed bound. Numbers: Source: /home/user/pnp-general/ath_prompts/measure/cost_per_result.md. The linear fit over 18 Sonnet seats in seat order gives a slope of +1,523 tokens per seat, with r = 0.22.
